pillars.importText: Streaming parser, content hashing and one transaction per run. A truncated or suspicious feed fails safely and never mass-deactivates listings.
pillars.dataTitle: PostgreSQL as the source of truth
pillars.dataText: SQL migrations, constraints, PostGIS radius search and row-level security. The browser only ever gets a read-only key.
pillars.i18nText: Locale-prefixed URLs with hreflang alternates. Descriptions come from the feed's own language nodes and fall back to English, clearly marked.

Pipeline.metaDescription: Read-only status of the Kyero-compatible XML import runs behind this demo.
Pipeline.title: Import pipeline
Pipeline.intro: The catalogue is filled by a command-line importer that reads a Kyero-style XML feed, validates it and upserts it into PostgreSQL. This page shows the most recent runs. It is read-only: imports cannot be triggered from the web.

how.fetch: Checksum and size limit are checked before anything is parsed.
how.parse: The whole feed is streamed and validated before any write; a truncated file fails here and existing data stays untouched.
how.upsert: Listings are upserted by (source, id) in one transaction. A content hash decides inserted / updated / unchanged, so re-running the same feed changes nothing.
how.guard: Kyero feeds are full snapshots, but missing listings are only reported, not removed. Soft deactivation needs an explicit flag and is refused when the record count drops sharply.
how.lock: A database advisory lock prevents two runs for the same source at once.

Pipeline.simulator: A scheduled job on a Linux VPS runs the importer daily against a simulated feed in which a few prices change, so new runs show real updates.

About.metaDescription: What is real, what is simulated and what is not implemented in the PropertyFlow technical demo.
About.title: About this demo
About.intro: PropertyFlow is a technical proof of concept for a Spanish real-estate catalogue. It exists to show an end-to-end pipeline, from an XML property feed to a bilingual public website, built with production habits: migrations, tests, least-privilege access and safe failure modes.
real: Next.js 16 site on Vercel reading live from Supabase PostgreSQL
SQL migrations with constraints, PostGIS geography and row-level security
Kyero V3-compatible XML importer with streaming parser, content hashing and idempotent upserts
Feed-level safety: truncated, malformed or DOCTYPE/XXE feeds are rejected; mass deactivation is guarded
Unit and PostgreSQL integration tests in GitHub Actions
simulated: All listings, prices, coordinates and descriptions are generated by a deterministic script
Photos are random placeholders from Lorem Picsum and do not show the listed homes
The XML feed follows the public Kyero V3 structure but is not a real agency or MLS feed
not: No real MLS, Kyero, Rightmove or CRM integration and no provider certification
No enquiries, accounts or agent back office
No production load testing; the dataset is a few hundred listings
About.arch: XML feed → importer (Node.js CLI on a Linux VPS, systemd timer) → Supabase PostgreSQL + PostGIS → Next.js on Vercel (read-only publishable key) → EN/DE catalogue.
About.source: The repository contains the migrations, fixtures, importer, tests, CI workflow and deployment notes.
About.kyero: Feed structure reference: Kyero XML Import Specification V3.9.1. Kyero-compatible does not mean Kyero-certified.
